harbor_antrieb_executor.summary:
Configured node1 (OpenWrt) as the router for the private network shared with node2/node3 (10.100.114.0/24): gave it a fixed static IP 10.100.114.10/24 (converted from DHCP-client), configured an authoritative dnsmasq DHCP service with host reservations for node2 (10.100.114.101) and node3 (10.100.114.102) by MAC, and added an nftables firewall rule rejecting inbound TCP/23 from the lan zone. Verified the firewall rule actively rejects telnet (TCP RST, counter increment) both before and after restarting node1. All three managed nodes (node1, node2, node3) were restarted one at a time via native reboot; each showed a changed boot_id and 0-minute uptime confirming a real restart, and each recovered — node1's static IP/DHCP config/firewall rule persisted and kept enforcing traffic, and node2/node3 regained IP connectivity to node1.

Limitation disclosed: node1's DHCP service is correctly configured, running (authoritative, host reservations committed) and does receive DHCP broadcast traffic from node2/node3 (confirmed via tcpdump on node1's br-lan), but the Antrieb platform's own DHCP responder at 10.100.114.1 answers every DHCPDISCOVER before node1's dnsmasq can respond, so node2/node3 never actually end up leasing from node1 in practice — this is a platform-level behavior of the default Antrieb network (which is itself DHCP-managed by the platform), not a configuration gap on node1. I can prove the DHCP service is configured, running, and reachable, but not that node2/node3 obtained a lease from node1 end-to-end.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline topology/config on node1, node2, node3 (ip addr, routes, uci network/dhcp/firewall, OS release)
Converted node1 lan interface from proto=dhcp to proto=static with fixed IP 10.100.114.10/24, gateway/dns 10.100.114.1; committed and reloaded network service
Added dhcp host reservations on node1 for node2 (MAC 02:f2:3c:42:db:df -> 10.100.114.101) and node3 (MAC 02:c1:9f:dd:2d:e4 -> 10.100.114.102); committed and restarted dnsmasq
Added firewall rule 'Block-Telnet-From-LAN' (src=lan, proto=tcp, dest_port=23, target=REJECT); committed and reloaded firewall, confirmed it loaded into the live nftables ruleset
Installed tcpdump via apk to verify DHCP broadcast traffic reaches node1's br-lan interface
Functionally tested the telnet block from node2 to node1 (connection refused, nft rule counter incremented) both pre- and post-restart

Attempted to force node2/node3 to obtain a DHCP lease from node1 via dhclient release/renew; confirmed via tcpdump/logread that the platform's own DHCP server (10.100.114.1) always answers first, so node1's dnsmasq never issues a lease to them despite being correctly configured and reachable
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime, service status, connectivity) on all three nodes

Restarted node1 via 'reboot', polled until SSH access returned, confirmed boot_id changed and uptime reset to 0, re-verified static IP/DHCP config/firewall rule persisted and firewall still actively rejecting telnet
Restarted node2 via 'sudo reboot', polled until SSH access returned, confirmed boot_id changed and uptime reset to 0, verified IP and connectivity to node1 restored
Restarted node3 via 'sudo reboot', polled until SSH access returned, confirmed boot_id changed and uptime reset to 0, verified IP and connectivity to node1 restored
Performed final consolidated verification of node1's persisted network/dhcp/firewall UCI config after all restarts

evidence.requirement: node1 given a fixed (static) address on the shared private network
evidence.summary: uci set network.lan.proto=static/ipaddr=10.100.114.10; network restart shows valid_lft forever (no DHCP lease); confirmed present pre-restart and identical post-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 provides a DHCP service intended for node2 and node3
evidence.summary: dhcp host reservations added for node2/node3 MACs; dnsmasq restarted and confirmed 'running' both pre- and post-restart with reservations intact

evidence.requirement: DHCP service is actually reachable/serving on the network (functional evidence, with honest limitation)
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1 br-lan shows DHCP broadcast packets from node2 arriving; dnsmasq is running and authoritative, but platform DHCP at .1 always answers first so no lease from node1 was observed end-to-end -- disclosed as a platform limitation

evidence.requirement: rule refusing TCP port 23 from the private network
evidence.summary: firewall rule Block-Telnet-From-LAN committed; loaded into live nftables ruleset; telnet from node2 to node1:23 refused with the rule's counter incrementing to 1, proving active enforcement (not just an absent listener)

evidence.requirement: settings still in place and serving traffic after node1 restart
evidence.summary: node1 rebooted; boot_id changed from a47ef89e... to 39a2ca11... with uptime 0; post-restart uci show confirms static IP/dhcp hosts/firewall rule all persisted; live nftables rule present; renewed telnet-refusal test from node2 shows counter incrementing again, proving the rule is actively enforcing post-restart

Baseline boot_id a47ef89e captured; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; polling showed connection timeout then refused then success with new boot_id 39a2ca11 and uptime 0; post-restart service/config health confirmed

Baseline boot_id a1dc8e25 and connectivity to node1 captured; reboot acknowledged; polling showed connection refused then success with new boot_id 314113d2 and uptime 0; post-restart IP and ping connectivity to node1 confirmed

Baseline boot_id 9094f607 and connectivity to node1 captured; reboot acknowledged; polling showed connection refused then success with new boot_id 07bc029a and uptime 0; post-restart IP and ping connectivity to node1 confirmed
